html:
The Nivaclé are an Indigenous people of the Gran Chaco, the hot dry plain along the Pilcomayo River. About 13,700 live in the Presidente Hayes and Boquerón departments of Paraguay, and some 200 in Argentina. Their language belongs to the Mataco-Mataguayo family, related to that of the Wichí.

They were hunters, fishers and gatherers who also grew small gardens, and moved with the seasons along the river. Their neighbours included the Enxet, the Qom and the Ayoreo.

The Chaco War between Bolivia and Paraguay, from 1932 to 1935, was fought across their land. Afterwards Catholic missions and Mennonite farming colonies grew up in the region, and many Nivaclé settled near them or worked on their farms.
